edits.name: the skee-ball lane in the back-right corner
edits.prompt: This is a crop of an approved hand-painted watercolour game painting of a cozy arcade, with one flat-colour block-out added in the room's right corner: a child-sized skee-ball lane whose tall purple hood stands with its back against the brick wall, and whose long teal ramp runs from it toward the lower left. The second image shows this skee-ball lane's design. Repaint ONLY the block-out as that finished skee-ball lane in the painting's soft watercolour and thin warm-brown ink style: the tall rounded purple hood, its cream target face with brown rings and a dark centre hole between two yellow posts, facing the lower left; the long teal ramp with yellow side rails on a purple base, sloping down to a small purple foot end at the lower left. Keep the block-out's exact position, outline, size, and perspective, standing on the same floor tiles, with a soft contact shadow on the floor. The soft blurred smudge on the wall and floor around the hood's top and right is where three gumball machines on stands were taken away: there, paint the brick wall, the wall's base, the floor tiles, and the claw machine's right side exactly as they continue around it, with no gumball machines anywhere. Change nothing else: every floor tile, every line, the claw machine, the ticket counter, the bricks, the stars, and the string lights stay exactly as they are, pixel for pixel. No text anywhere.

edits.name: the red gumball machine at the front corner
edits.prompt: This is a crop of an approved hand-painted watercolour game painting of a cozy arcade floor, with one flat-colour block-out added near the floor's front corner: a red gumball machine standing on the checkerboard. It faces away from us, into the room, so we see its back: from this side the red body is smooth and plain all the way down. Keep its exact position, outline, size, and perspective, standing on the same tiles. Give it a soft contact shadow on the floor. Change nothing else: every floor tile, every line, and the floor's front edge stay exactly as they are, pixel for pixel. No text anywhere.
